sanskrit: āṅgiraso janmanāsi tam u tvāhur vanaspate | sa pīlo rakṣo bādhasva sākam indreṇa medinā ||
english: By birth thou art of the Āṅgirasa lineage — so they call thee, O lord of the forest. Do thou, the Pīlu tree, drive off the rākṣasas together with Indra the ally.

sanskrit: apa rakṣāṃsi bādhasva bādhasva parirāpiṇaḥ | piśācān pīlo kravyādo bādhasva mūradevinaḥ ||
english: Drive away the rākṣasas, drive away those that prowl about; O Pīlu, drive away the piśācas, the flesh-devouring, the ill-omened ones.

sanskrit: yayāhus tṛṣṭaṃ kaṭukam apagūḍhaṃ phale kulam | tasyai hiraṇyakeśyai namaḥ kṛṇmo arātaye ||
english: She of whom they speak — whose fruit-cluster is bitter, pungent, and hidden away — to that golden-haired one, Arāti, we pay homage.

sanskrit: yā mahatī mahonmānā sarvā āśā vyānaśe | tasyai hiraṇyakeśyai namaḥ kṛṇmo arātaye ||
english: She who, vast and of great measure, has pervaded all the quarters of space — to that golden-haired one, Arāti, we pay homage.

sanskrit: yas te yoniṃ pratireḍhy āṇḍādo garbhadūṣaṇaḥ | arāyaṃ putraṃ prāpī yas taṃ pīluḥ sahatām itaḥ ||
english: Whoever licks at thy womb, the devourer of eggs, the corrupter of embryos — may the Pīlu tree smite from here that miserly one who would take thy son.

sanskrit: yadā pīlav āṅgirasa pakvo 'tiṣṭho vanaspate | athāhur indraṃ jajñānaṃ śakraṃ barjahye prati ||
english: When thou, O Pīlu of Āṅgirasa lineage, stood ripened, O lord of the forest — then they proclaimed Indra born, mighty Śakra, facing Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: yathā sedim abādhathāḥ pacyamāno vanaspate | evā pīlo rakṣo bādhasva sākam indreṇa medinā ||
english: As thou didst press back the furrow while ripening, O lord of the forest — even so, O Pīlu tree, drive off the rākṣasas together with Indra the ally.

sanskrit: yat piśācaiḥ puruṣasya jagdhaṃ bhavaty ātmanaḥ | ā pīlo pyāyate punas tava cāśnāti pippalam ||
english: Whatever of a man's own self has been consumed by piśācas — the Pīlu tree restores it again, and he eats of thy berry.

sanskrit: pīluṃ tvāhuḥ pīvaṃ tvāhur atho tvāhur vanaspatim | sarvā te bhadrā nāmāni tebhir naḥ pāhy aṃhasaḥ ||
english: They call thee Pīlu; they call thee the fat one; they also call thee lord of the forest. All thy names are auspicious — with them do thou guard us from distress.

sanskrit: rakṣohaṇaṃ vṛtrahaṇaṃ pīluṃ piśācajambhanam | jajñānam agre vṛkṣāṇāṃ taṃ te badhnāmy āyuṣe ||
english: The Pīlu — slayer of rākṣasas, slayer of Vṛtra, crusher of piśācas — born first among trees: thee I bind upon thee for long life.
